title: Rink in the Park roof replacement and heritage register deadline
subtitle: Also: accessible parking, traffic and parking by-laws, a 630-unit subdivision public meeting, and an all-way stop request.
overview: Council awarded the Rink in the Park roof replacement tender to T.P. Crawford Limited for a total of $1,583,080.32 {{vote:m6}}. Staff said the original roof leaks and is pitted, and that the arena still has useful life. The work will also replace insulation and prepare the structure for possible future solar panels.

Council asked the Mayor to write to the Premier of Ontario seeking a five-year extension, to 2030, of the deadline for designating the 152 listed heritage properties in Waterloo {{vote:m7}}. Without designation, properties come off the municipal register on January 1, 2025. Council also approved changes to the Accessible Parking By-law for the Uptown Parkade {{vote:m3}} and to the Traffic and Parking and Parking Administrative Monetary Penalties by-laws {{vote:m5}}. It received the Joint Services Initiative Committee update for information {{vote:m4}}.

In an informal public meeting, council heard about a proposed subdivision of up to 630 units at 400 Millennium Boulevard. No decision was made, and staff will report back. Council also met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes record no public report from it.

decisions.item: Rink in the Park roof replacement
decisions.detail: Council awarded tender RFT24-02 to T.P. Crawford Limited for a total of $1,583,080.32 including unrecoverable HST and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the agreement.
Council asked the Mayor to write to the Premier and others requesting that the deadline for designating listed heritage properties be extended from January 1, 2025 to January 1, 2030.
Council approved report CAO2024-011 and amendments to Accessible Parking By-Law #09-106 relating to the Uptown Parkade.
Council approved amendments to the Traffic and Parking By-law and the Parking Administrative Monetary Penalties By-law, including provisions for regulated parking events.
Council received the 2023 update on joint services work with Kitchener for information.

debate: A resident asked for all-way stops at Mayfield Avenue and Renaud Drive after reported near-misses. Staff said a 2023 study found the traffic-volume and collision thresholds were not met. They added that an unwarranted all-way stop can increase collisions and create a false sense of security. A review of the area is expected next year.

On the roof, one councillor asked why replace it now rather than wait to redesign the facility. Staff said assessments showed remaining useful life, the leaks were near critical, and no redevelopment was likely within the budget cycle. Councillors also raised greenhouse gas reductions and accessibility at the front entrance, which staff said would be handled separately.

On the Millennium Boulevard subdivision, several delegates raised traffic. They cited all access points opening onto Millennium Boulevard, event congestion near Rim Park, and the single-lane bridge on Country Squire Road. Councillors asked staff about the lack of access onto Country Squire Road. Staff said transportation comments were still pending.

The applicant's representative said the traffic study found no new signal or roundabout was required and recommended extending a right-turn lane. A delegate from a climate group urged net-zero homes, transit passes and less gas use. Councillors also asked about the loss of employment land, schools, and district energy.

On heritage, councillors said the motion might not win a full five-year extension but was worth asking for. Staff said about 46 priority properties had been identified, and no firm timeline existed for reviewing all of them.
